plan.title: Implement pseudoterminal autoplay for single-path workflow transitions
plan.overview: Create a TypeScript pseudoterminal class that spawns the Claude CLI, intercepts output to detect [KANBAN_COMPLETE] markers, and triggers automatic workflow transitions for single-path statuses. The pseudoterminal replaces the existing terminal.capability.ts usage for kanban commands, while autoplay orchestration logic lives in extension.ts following the capability-computer separation pattern.

approach.rationale:
The existing compiled pseudoterminal at apps/vscode/out/terminal/kanban-terminal.js provides the implementation pattern: VSCode Pseudoterminal interface with writeEmitter/closeEmitter, child_process.spawn for CLI execution, and output buffer for marker detection.
Architecture follows three-layer separation: - Pseudoterminal (new capability): I/O mechanism for process spawning and output interception - task-actions.computer.ts: Pure logic for determining if status is single-path - extension.ts (orchestrator): Policy for when to auto-trigger, status bar management
The pseudoterminal provides an onComplete callback rather than returning promises, allowing the orchestrator to chain actions. Exit code checking stops autoplay on failures.

change.new: createKanbanTerminal + onComplete callback pattern for kanban commands
change.affects: extension.ts command handlers (kanban.runAction, kanban.runGlobalAction, kanban.startDiscovery, kanban.createTask, kanban.runNextAction)

case.scenario: [KANBAN_COMPLETE] in middle of output, not end

edge-cases.case: Buffer captures last 4000 chars; marker detection uses includes(), so position doesn't matter

case.scenario: Claude CLI exits before marker output

edge-cases.case: Process close handler fires, onComplete receives exit code, autoplay stops on non-zero

case.scenario: Task file doesn't exist when re-reading

edge-cases.case: Wrap in try-catch, stop autoplay if parse fails

case.scenario: User rapidly closes and reopens terminal

edge-cases.case: Terminal close handler clears autoplayTerminal reference; new terminal starts fresh
autoplayTaskId tracks current task; new trigger overwrites, only one chain runs
